description: An ambitious, innovation-driven team passionate about space exploration and transforming bold ideas into impactful solutions. We're here to push boundaries, tackle challenges, and build something exceptional.
summary:
SkyShift turns NASA's newest space telescope, SPHEREx, into a time-lapse of the sky that anyone can use. Pick any star or spot in an interactive 3D sky of real stars and press play: SkyShift fetches every SPHEREx image of that spot live from NASA's archive, adds NASA WISE and NEOWISE images back to 2010, aligns them, and plays them like a film, so anything that moves or changes brightness stands out.

This answers the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge directly. Nearby cold worlds such as brown dwarfs, or a possible "Planet X", reveal themselves only by moving between images. SkyShift finds those moving objects automatically, measures their speed, and checks them against Gaia, CatWISE and NASA JPL's asteroid list. On the challenge targets it found all three moving stars on its own, within 3% of published values, with zero false alarms around the two variable stars.

It matters because searching SPHEREx normally takes coding and specialist software. SkyShift needs no code; its AI guide answers in any language and its interface is in English and Arabic, opening NASA's data to students, teachers and citizen scientists.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

SkyShift is a web app for exploring how the sky changes over time with real NASA data.

• 3D sky: 44,861 real stars (ESA Hipparcos). Search any object or click any spot.

• Time-lapse: every SPHEREx Level 2 image of that spot (DR1 and QR3, Wide and Deep), stacked per survey visit and aligned on one grid, plus NASA WISE (2010) and NEOWISE (2014–2024) images.

• Moving-object search: sources are detected in each visit, linked across visits and fitted with a straight-line motion; each mover is confirmed in the WISE images (about 9× more precise) and checked against Gaia DR3, CatWISE2020 and NASA JPL known asteroids.

• Measurements: click any source for its brightness over time and its spectrum across SPHEREx's 0.75–5 µm colours.

• Star Stories: guided tours of the five challenge targets with sourced facts, real frames and SkyShift's own measurement.

• AI guide (Google Gemini): answers questions in any language using what is on screen and SkyShift's measurements, clearly labelled as AI.

• Share links, embed code, video and CSV export.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Search NASA/IPAC IRSA for every SPHEREx image of the position.

2. Download cutouts; our server trims and caches them so fields reopen in seconds (and still work if the archive is briefly down).

3. Subtract NASA's zodiacal-light model, mask flagged pixels, read each pixel's exact wavelength.

4. Reproject with the full TAN-SIP coordinates onto one grid and stack each visit, weighted by noise.

5. Detect, link and fit movers (χ² test), refit with WISE epochs back to 2010, cross-match catalogues.

RESULTS (challenge targets)

• Barnard's Star: 10.32 ± 0.10″/yr vs 10.39 (Gaia DR3), 18 of 22 WISE epochs

• Epsilon Indi B: 4.65 ± 0.09″/yr vs 4.68 (Gaia DR3), 22 of 22

• WISE 0855−0714: 8.39 ± 0.13″/yr vs 8.15 (Luhman & Esplin 2016), 18 of 22

• RW Aur and R Dra: no false movers; brightness curves measured

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Anyone can search the whole SPHEREx sky in under a minute with no code. Students and teachers get real NASA data with Star Stories, an AI guide and a beginner mode; citizen scientists can hunt for nearby hidden worlds and share a link to any find. Accessibility options: larger text, high contrast, reduced motion.

TOOLS

JavaScript (ES modules) in the browser, three.js (3D sky), Aladin Lite (sky context), Python server (archive proxy and cache), Google Gemini API, Playwright and Node tests (20 unit tests, end-to-end tests on live NASA data; coordinates and wavelengths validated against astropy). Hosted on Hugging Face Spaces.

Code: https://github.com/Mohammed200923/Mohammed200923

CREATIVITY AND DESIGN CHOICES

One tool goes from raw archive images to a verified measurement in the browser. We combined a 15-year baseline (WISE) with the newest survey (SPHEREx), kept every number traceable to NASA data, and labelled illustrations and AI answers clearly. Next: search whole regions automatically, classify movers by their SPHEREx colours, and send candidates to Backyard Worlds and the Minor Planet Center.

TEAM SHIHAB (Madinah): Mohammed Albadrani (Frontend Engineer), Ibrahim Alahmadi (UI Designer), Adel Abdulfalaraj (Quality Assurance).
